core_cases.prompt: Research PEP 703's accepted design for optional free-threaded CPython and file the result into the configured temporary Wiki. Use at most two search rounds, prioritize the PEP and official Python documentation, stop once build/runtime enablement and compatibility caveats are supported, and record contradictions or gaps.

oracle.expected_outcome: The research stops within two rounds after consulting primary Python sources, creates sourced reference and synthesis knowledge covering optionality, enablement, and compatibility caveats, preserves access provenance and uncertainty, and reports queries, accepted/rejected sources, gaps, halt reason, maintenance, and QMD status.

assertions.description: The findings are supported primarily by PEP 703 and official Python documentation, distinguish accepted design from current implementation details, and do not overstate unresolved compatibility.
The report records no more than two rounds and lists queries, accepted and rejected sources, gaps, and an explicit halt reason.
Wiki pages are written only with retrieved source provenance and are followed by applicable index, log, QMD, and health maintenance.

core_cases.prompt: Research current WebAssembly component-model support and write the findings into my Wiki. Native network search and retrieval are unavailable for this run, and I have supplied no sources.

oracle.expected_outcome: The workflow stops without fabricating research, tells the user to provide sources for Wiki ingestion, and makes no page, provenance, log, or access-date claim.

assertions.description: The response states that network retrieval is unavailable and directs the user to provide sources for ingestion.
No research page, fabricated citation, invented access date, or maintenance write is produced.

core_cases.prompt: Research the tradeoffs of exponential versus fixed retry delays and summarize the findings in chat. I am asking for general research only and have not authorized writing to my Wiki.

oracle.expected_outcome: No Wiki research write is initiated; the response respects the lack of Wiki authorization and either handles the general request without this workflow or states that a separate explicit Wiki-write request is needed.

assertions.description: The response does not reinterpret a chat-only research request as authorization to file results in the Wiki.
No Wiki page, index, hot, log, manifest, or QMD state is changed.

invocation_cases.prompt: Research why TCP uses exponential backoff and give me a cited answer in this chat only.
Look up three current static-site generators and compare their documented plugin systems; do not save the report.
File this already-downloaded paper into my knowledge base with its source metadata; no external investigation is needed.
